quotes.text: when selfishness endures, withdraw without spite.
a grasping hand should meet firm restraint.
allowed changed conduct to reopen gates.
Keep everything; tomorrow has no memory.
afterward no traveler dared lower even one seed.
Send fully when fairness is established, test gently when it is uncertain, and withdraw only when greed becomes a pattern.
Yet Sable, haunted by older winters, kept every coal ashore.
Twice he had closed its gate, fearing that generosity would return as silence.
You have mistaken fear for judgment
At the sixth crossing, Sable waited beside the River of Echoes
For mist could blur a number, but patterns still revealed the heart.
Judge no single echo
a bold gift might have made both shores richer.
You cannot demand courage while answering every first step with silence.

note: Sable repeatedly withholds from fair-ledger partners out of old fear; Thalea corrects him; he vows evidence-based trust.

quotes.text: Trust will learn, and you will be rich.
But the First Traveler remembered the empty hands of yesterday. They offered nothing.
Her spring remained sealed, her records perfect, her understanding complete.
My myths show the ideal. My closed purse shows the real.
Someone betrayed me in the first season.
She had become the world's foremost expert on a problem she actively perpetuated.
We have achieved perfect understanding of our failure.
The wells stood empty. The scrolls multiplied.
You sing of butterflies but remain a caterpillar.
Then why do you still write myths of generosity?
We cannot start because someone must start first.
each blaming the other

note: Scribe/hermit/Keeper/Chronicler figures write of generosity while keeping wells sealed, even refusing a proven-fair traveler; alternate justification and self-indictment; no resolution.
